title: Much, Many and A Lot Of
summary: Learn how to talk about quantities in English. Discover when to use much, many, and a lot of.

sections.p: We use 'a lot of' when we have a big quantity of something. The great thing about 'a lot of' is that you can use it with both countable nouns (like apples or friends) and uncountable nouns (like water or money). It is very common in everyday English, especially in positive sentences.

ex.en: I have a lot of friends.
She drinks a lot of water every day.
ex.mean: She drinks a big amount of water.

ex.en: We need a lot of time for this project.

sections.p: We use 'many' with countable nouns. Countable nouns are things you can count as separate items, like books, cars, chairs, or apples. We usually use 'many' in questions and negative sentences, but not very often in positive sentences.

ex.en: How many brothers do you have?
ex.mean: Asking about the number of brothers.

ex.en: I don't have many books at home.
ex.mean: I have a small number of books.

ex.en: Are there many restaurants in this town?
ex.mean: Asking if there are a big number of restaurants.

sections.p: We use 'much' with uncountable nouns. Uncountable nouns are things we cannot count individually, like water, money, time, milk, or sugar. Just like 'many', we usually use 'much' in negative sentences and questions, rather than in positive sentences.

ex.en: How much money do you need?
ex.mean: Asking about the amount of money.

ex.en: I don't have much time today.
ex.mean: I have a small amount of time.

ex.en: Is there much sugar in this coffee?
ex.mean: Asking about the amount of sugar.

tip: Remember: 'Many' is for things you can count one by one (many cats). 'Much' is for things you measure (much milk). 'A lot of' works for both in positive sentences!

quiz.en: I have ___ of homework to do tonight.
How ___ apples do we need for the pie?
She doesn't drink ___ coffee in the evening.
There are ___ nice people in my English class.
How ___ time do we have before the train leaves?
I don't have ___ friends in this new city yet.
